newsitem.title: LEBANON: U.S. travel ban on Lebanon justified-envoy.
newsitem.headline: U.S. travel ban on Lebanon justified-envoy.

text.p: An 11-year-old U.S. ban on Americans travelling to Lebanon was still justified because of possible threats to their safety, U.S. ambassador Richard Jones said on Friday.

"I understand that the American travel ban is an obstacle to the kind of participation for American companies in the Lebanese economy that I would like to see. But it is an obstacle that we feel up until now has been unfortunately justified by the security situation for Americans in Lebanon," Jones said.
The ban, reviewed every six months by the State Department, was imposed in 1985 during the 1975-90 civil war after Moslem militants hijacked a U.S. airliner to Beirut and shot a passenger.
U.S. Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau said in February Lebanon remained a haven for armed groups with a history of attacks on Americans, like the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God).
But Lebanese officials said at the time that extending the ban was unjustified, arguing that Beirut was safer for Americans than some U.S. cities.

Speaking to reporters at the foreign ministry, Jones said he has been trying since being posted to Lebanon last year to promote closer economic ties between the United States and Lebanon despite the travel ban.
"I think that there is a lot that can be done now that will benefit our commercial relationship and develop it in Lebanon before even the ban is lifted," Jones added.
The ban was relaxed last year to allow travel for family reunification and family emergencies.
